text.p: Overseas Union Bank Ltd should report better profits for the second half of 1996 than in the first half of the year, president and chief executive officer Peter Seah said on Friday.

Seah told Reuters in an interview the bank had done well in the first half of 1996, coming in with a 22.3 percent year-on-year rise in net profit at Singapore $142.15 million for the six months to June 30, 1996.
"I expect our second half numbers in absolute terms to be better than the first half," he said.

But Seah added that, in terms of percentage growth year-on-year, the overall increase for the second half of the year was "pretty difficult to estimate at this point in time because we had a good second half also in 1995".
Asked if he accepted The Estimate Directory's latest average forecast by banking analysts of 20 percent year-on-year growth for OUB in 1996 as a whole, Seah replied:
"I wouldn't want to give an estimate, but it would be nice."
Seah said he thought OUB, one of Singapore's four main banks with total assets at the end of 1995 of S$25.63 billion, would "do well for the whole of 1996".

"How well would also depend on how well the stockmarket performs because that would lead to greater contributions from our stockbroking operations and more income from fund management and corporate finance activities," he said.
"So I can't give you a number, or percentage, but I would say we are quite comfortable that 1996 will be a reasonable year for the bank," Seah said.
